units.title: Trigonometric identities and equations
units.why: Identities allow equivalent forms to be proved and equations to be solved across an interval.
principles: solutions repeat by the function period
examples: Worked example — Foundation: identify the known values in a Trigonometry problem, write the relevant rule (sin²θ+cos²θ=1), substitute carefully, then check the result against the question.

Worked example — Standard: compare two representations of identities and equations and explain which features stay constant. State the rule first, show the substitution or construction, and interpret the answer in context.

Worked example — Challenge: solve a new trigonometry problem by naming the unknown, selecting a valid method, showing each algebraic step, and checking the final result with an independent representation.
misconceptions: giving only one solution on a full interval
dividing by an expression that may be zero
